messages.subject: Communication errors with statet server
messages.body_plain:
Hello

After upgrading to eclipse 4.4.2 and Statet 3.4.1 on OS X I started having troubles to use the Statet server on a remote linux machine.
I can instantiate an R session, which initially works fine, but after some stage I receive Communication errors and also Java heap space errors (despite 8g allocated..). When this occurs, typically also the console starts displaying lots of funny characters. The RJ server log looks clean and I have tried different java versions on that end. So my suspicion would be that this is an issue on the eclipse client side. Any ideas what could cause this? rj and rjserver is up to date (version 2.x)

Cheers

Moritz

messages.subject: Re: Communication errors with statet server
messages.body_plain:
Hi Stefan

I have tried R-3.0.2 and a fresh build of R-3.1.2 on the server side, as well as different
JDKs (jdk1.7.0_07, jdk1.7.0_25, jdk1.7.0_71, jdk1.8.0_11) on the ubuntu server (Ubuntu 12.04.3 LTS). 
I have also tried a fresh install of eclipse (4.4.2.M20150204-1700) on the client end without success.

The problem can be attenuated by disabling 'Refresh DB automatically' in the 
Console tab of the Run Configuration and triggered by manually refreshing the DB. Is the object DB
linked to the R environment on the client computer? So could the problem be caused by incompatibilities
of the remote and local R environments?

I'm trying to come up with steps for reproducing the errors for the server R session. It appears to mostly
after rather involved computations (which is why I run them on a server) generating an R session 
of about 10-20G with about 500 objects, usually large data.frames or arrays. The script causing problems is a bit
too complicated to share here (but works fine in a stand-alone R session and prior versions of statet), and I'm rerunning the analysis now step-by-step to find out where exactly the problems arise.

Regards,
Moritz

Hi Moritz,

[2015-03-04 14:09] Moritz Gerstung wrote:
> Hi Stefan

> tried a fresh install of eclipse (4.4.2.M20150204-1700) on the client
> end without success.
>
> The problem can be attenuated by disabling 'Refresh DB automatically'
> in the Console tab of the Run Configuration and triggered by manually
> refreshing the DB. Is the object DB linked to the R environment on
> the client computer? So could the problem be caused by
> incompatibilities of the remote and local R environments?

The object DB is linked to your R console (a single session) and shown 
in the object browser.
If the R package and jar for RJ server are up-to-date, then it is 
probably just a bug in RJ/StatET.

>
> I'm trying to come up with steps for reproducing the errors for the
> server R session. It appears to mostly after rather involved
> computations (which is why I run them on a server) generating an R
> session of about 10-20G with about 500 objects, usually large
> data.frames or arrays. The script causing problems is a bit too
> complicated to share here (but works fine in a stand-alone R session
> and prior versions of statet), and I'm rerunning the analysis now
> step-by-step to find out where exactly the problems arise.

I think it is a special type / structure of object which causes the 
problem.  Maybe you reproduce the problem with a single object of your 
generated result and you can share such an object (saved R data)?

Regards,
Stephan
